problem: Existing VLN policies reason only over past and current observations and treat recorded future frames merely as later inputs, so they miss action-conditioned visual dynamics and act myopically. Explicit world-model or imagination pipelines add extra predictors and inference cost and suffer from compounding errors and policy-model mismatch.
motivation: Navigation is interactive: each action changes what is observed next, so anticipating near-future views should improve decisions and reduce backtracking and collisions. Future frames are available in offline training trajectories, so they can serve as training-only privileged supervision while inference stays strictly causal.
key_idea: Train a VLM navigator with a step-propagated continuous latent (the Pilot Token) that is regressed to the pooled visual feature of the next-next frame, teacher-forced with the next frame, so it internalizes lookahead without future frames or an external world model at inference.
insight: Supervising the Pilot Token with future visual features is what matters: the ablation shows that no extra supervision (SR 51.7), 3D VGGT targets (50.3) or text targets (53.2) give little or negative gain on R2R-CE val-unseen, versus 62.0 with vision targets. Internalized imagination also beats plug-in video world models (Wan2.1, CogVideoX) in SR and is far cheaper (130 ms vs 2040-5460 ms per action). PCA shows the tokens do not collapse and cluster by action, and PilotLoop rounds improve SR and SPL steadily.
method: Pilot Token recurrence: a latent z_t, produced from the LLM's hidden state at a dedicated placeholder slot by a linear Pilot module, is cached and fed into the same slot at the next step. The input is [instruction; current visual tokens; PILOT(z_{t-1})], and a PilotCache read/write at inference means no extra computation.
Backbone: SigLIP-initialized vision encoder and a 7B LLaVA-Video LLM on monocular RGB. Actions FWD/LEFT/RIGHT/STOP are decoded by the LLM output head.

Two-step future privilege: in training the Pilot slot is filled with the mean-pooled vision latent of o_{t+1} (teacher forcing), and the predicted z_t is regressed with an MSE loss to the pooled latent of o_{t+2}. The total loss is L_act + 0.1 L_pil.

PilotLoop flywheel: a DAgger-style loop of on-policy rollout collection, expert takeover (Habitat shortest-path follower) when the agent deviates too far, target construction, and fine-tuning, repeated for several rounds after imitation bootstrapping.
Training data: R2R, RxR, EnvDrop-augmented R2R on MP3D, plus ScaleVLN trajectories on HM3D. Rollouts use 16x RTX 4090 and training uses 8x A100.
Inference: strictly causal, using the current frame, instruction and cached Pilot Token; no future frames or world-model rollout.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-Video-7B with SigLIP vision encoder (fine-tuned end-to-end) plus a linear Pilot module
setting.training_data: R2R, RxR, EnvDrop-augmented R2R (MP3D) and ScaleVLN synthesized HM3D trajectories; imitation bootstrap followed by DAgger-style on-policy flywheel rounds with expert takeover
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (no depth, odometry or panorama)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete FWD / LEFT / RIGHT / STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE) and NVIDIA Isaac Lab (VLN-PE, Unitree H1 humanoid)
setting.privileged: none at test time (future frames are used only in training; the expert takes over during training rollouts)

numbers.extra: trained on R2R+RxR+EnvDrop+ScaleVLN with PilotLoop; monocular RGB only

numbers_note: The paper reports the VLN-PE Val-Seen NE as 4.10 (stored as 4.1). Ablation numbers on R2R-CE val-seen are only in the ablation tables. The PilotLoop curve is given only as a figure.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen LatentPilot reaches SR 62.0 / SPL 58.0 / NE 4.41, and on RxR-CE SR 58.2 / SPL 49.9 / nDTW 67.5, beating the strongest baseline JanusVLN (60.5/56.8; 56.2/47.5) using only monocular RGB. On VLN-PE val-unseen it gets SR 56.42 / SPL 47.74 versus DualVLN's 51.60 / 42.49, with lower fall and stuck rates.
limitations: Real-robot results are only qualitative (corridor demos), with no quantitative success rates.
Training is costly: 16 RTX 4090 GPUs for on-policy rollouts plus 8 A100 for training. Future supervision is mean-pooled to a single vector and covers only two steps ahead.
The paper does not clearly separate the effect of extra data (ScaleVLN, EnvDrop) from that of the method against baselines, and the ablations do not isolate the Pilot Token from the flywheel.
